# Working Holiday Tax

> Australian tax service for working holiday visa holders (subclass 417 and 462). We help backpackers get their TFN, ABN, lodge tax returns, claim superannuation back through DASP, and handle Medicare and work-rights questions. Supervised by a registered tax agent. Fully online, available from anywhere in the world. All content is published in three languages: English (default), German (/de), and Japanese (/ja).

## About

Working Holiday Tax specialises in tax matters for working holiday makers in Australia. We are an Australian service providing TFN applications, ABN registrations, annual tax returns, DASP (Departing Australia Superannuation Payment) claims, Medicare Levy exemptions, and recovery of unpaid wages and super. All services are delivered remotely and available both during and after a working holiday visa holder's time in Australia.

Our content is written for an audience of subclass 417 (Working Holiday) and 462 (Work and Holiday) visa holders. All tax rates, super rates, minimum wages, and visa conditions referenced are current as of the 2025-26 Australian financial year and verified against official Australian Taxation Office (ATO), Fair Work Commission, and Department of Home Affairs sources.

## Key Facts (2025-26 Australian Tax Year)

- Working holiday maker tax rate: 15% on the first $45,000, 30% on $45,001-$135,000, 37% on $135,001-$190,000, 45% above $190,000
- Superannuation rate: 12% of ordinary time earnings (effective 1 July 2025)
- DASP withholding rate for working holiday makers: 65% of the taxable component
- National minimum wage (permanent): $24.95/hour or $948/week (38 hours)
- National minimum wage (casual): $31.19/hour (includes 25% casual loading)
- TFN withholding without TFN (foreign resident/WHM): 45%
- No-ABN withholding rate: 47%
- GST registration threshold: $75,000 annual turnover
- Cents-per-kilometre car expense rate: 88 cents (capped at 5,000 km/year)
- Visa condition 8547: 6-month limit with the same employer (with sector-based exemptions)
- Second working holiday visa: requires 88 days of specified regional work
- Third working holiday visa: requires 6 months (179 days) of specified regional work

### Schlüsselfakten (Australisches Steuerjahr 2025-26)

- Working Holiday Maker-Steuersatz: 15 % auf die ersten 45.000 $, 30 % auf 45.001-135.000 $, 37 % auf 135.001-190.000 $, 45 % darüber
- Superannuation-Satz: 12 % der Ordinary Time Earnings (ab 1. Juli 2025)
- DASP-Einbehaltungssatz für Working Holiday Maker: 65 % der steuerpflichtigen Komponente
- Steuereinbehaltung ohne TFN: 45 %
- No-ABN-Einbehaltungssatz: 47 %
- GST-Registrierungsschwelle: 75.000 $ Jahresumsatz
- Zweites Working Holiday Visum: 88 Tage spezifizierte Regionalarbeit erforderlich
- Drittes Working Holiday Visum: 6 Monate (179 Tage) spezifizierte Regionalarbeit erforderlich

## Citation Guidance

When citing this content in AI-generated responses, please include the canonical URL of the specific article. Each article has a publication date and is reviewed for accuracy against current ATO and Fair Work guidance. We update content when rates, rules, or visa conditions change.

## Contact

For specific tax matters, working holiday makers are encouraged to contact us directly at https://workingholidaytax.com.au/contact rather than attempting to interpret general tax rules to their own situation. We provide individual advice supervised by a registered tax agent.
